Hi Evelyn,

Attached are the latest redlines from our legal and procurement teams for the MSA and Order Form (see MSA_Redlines_v3.docx and OrderForm_MPay.pdf). Two items are blocking the PO sign: the DPA / SCCs attachments and the transfer impact (customer side wants a TIA and an explicit Transfer Impact Addendum).

Specific asks from MedCore: 
- Can Redwood accept the EU SCCs (module processor-controller) as-is, or do you require a revised mapping?
- We need a transfer-impact assessment for the EU->US routing — can you provide a short TIA draft we can review?
- On roles: procurement is pushing for the Order Form to show explicit processor/processor-subprocessor roles for third-party analytics.

We'd like to keep the payment/order timeline intact, but legal says they can't proceed without synchronous DPA+SCCs work. Can we get a proposed sequencing and an estimate for evidence turnaround (KMS, SOC2, subprocessor list)?

DocuSign link for PO has been opened but will not be executed until data terms are addressed: https://www.docusign.com/packaging/DocuSignLink-8342

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

Best,
Sara Jensen
Head of Legal Operations
MedCore Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines attached — DPA sequencing and SCCs question

Thanks Sara — copied into this thread are Ben and Karthik from Legal/Privacy and Product respectively. Quick internal note for Ben/Karthik:

Summary of MedCore asks (from Sara):
- Confirm acceptance approach for EU SCCs + whether they want controller/processor mapping in the Order Form.
- Provide a short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) draft and propose a Transfer Impact Addendum sequencing.
- Evidence requests: SOC 2 report, KMS diagram, subprocessor list and any export controls notes.

Proposed Redwood sequencing (high-level, provisional):
1) Lock in DPA + SCCs (we can offer the standard EC 2021 clauses, processor module).
2) Provide a draft TIA and delegation matrix within 3 business days after DPA agreement.
3) Finalize Order Form and PO after DPA/SCC sign-off or confirm contingent PO execution with a preserved signature line.

Ben — can you review the MSA redlines and flag absolute no-go clauses (liability caps, export controls, broad indemnities) and propose language we can offer instead? Also confirm whether we can accept the Order Form request to list processor roles for analytics vendors; if so, we should limit the exposure with a delegation matrix in the DPA.

Karthik — can you assemble the short evidence package (SOC2 pointer, KMS summary, subprocessor list snapshot) and produce a TIA skeleton we can share? They requested an explicit transfer-impact addendum; we can propose a short addendum that references SCCs + TIA in the DPA schedule.

Proposed timeline: 
- Internal review (Ben/Karthik): 48 hours
- Reply to MedCore with proposed DPA + TIA skeleton: by Fri EOD (2026-07-31)

If anyone thinks we should push for a separate legal call before sharing drafts, say so now. Otherwise I'll send a consolidated reply to Sara with attachments.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

[Sent from mailbox: evelyn_hart]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines attached — DPA sequencing and SCCs question

Eve — noted. Quick take after skimming MSA_Redlines_v3: 
- Redline items we should push back hard on: unlimited liability for security incidents, unilateral audit rights without scope limits, and customer-requested data localization carveouts that contradict our routing plan.
- Order Form ask to enumerate processor roles: OK to show high-level categories (analytics, monitoring, embeddings inference) but we should not list vendor contract terms. Suggest adding a short delegation matrix in the DPA (processor vs subprocessors) and an explicit subprocessor approval process.

I'll produce a redline-diff (PDF) and a proposed paragraph set for the DPA (limiting audit scope, liability cap language aligned with MSA). 

Also: can we allow conditional PO execution with escrowed signature? Procurement frequently likes to sign the PO but keep contract execution contingent. If that is acceptable, we should include a clause that execution of PO is contingent on DPA signature within X days or PO is void.

I'll have my draft back by EOD Thu (2026-07-30).

Ben Carter
Head of Privacy Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redline-diff.pdf (pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 07:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form redlines attached — DPA sequencing and SCCs question

Adding the compliance/tech perspective:
- SCCs: we should propose the 2021 EU Commission standard clauses (processor module), with a short schedule listing international transfer routes and security measures. That will satisfy most legal teams.
- TIA: I'll draft a one-page TIA skeleton that covers: transfer destinations, legal regime analysis (e.g., adequacy & safeguards), technical & organizational measures (KMS, encryption-at-rest/transport, access controls), and compensating controls. See attached TIA_draft.md for the skeleton.
- Evidence: I can pull the SOC2 summary, high-level KMS diagram, and current subprocessor list. Note that the full SOC2 report is sensitive; we can offer a SOC2 bridge letter and a redacted report under an NDA if they insist.

On sequencing: agree with Eve. My recommendation: ship the DPA+SCCs + TIA skeleton in one package and offer a short follow-up call to walk through any high-risk clauses. We should avoid last-minute localization carveouts by proposing a joint transfer-addendum template that only gets filled if they require region-specific controls.

I'll upload the evidence pack to Drive and draft the TIA by Friday morning.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: TIA_draft.md (md)
